How to use this calculator

  1. Enter local date, local time, from time zone and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How time zone is calculated

Convert a local date and time between two named IANA time zones using their daylight-saving rules for that date. Results retain the destination’s local clock and UTC offset, and flag invalid zones or nonexistent local times rather than silently guessing. 09:00 in New York can map to different UTC offsets depending on the date because daylight saving changes. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Many regions change UTC offset seasonally; the selected date determines the applicable offset. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

Time Zone Calculator is calculated from the supplied measurement fields using the units shown.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why does the same conversion change by season?

Many regions change UTC offset seasonally; the selected date determines the applicable offset.

Which time-zone names work?

Use IANA identifiers such as Europe/Berlin or America/New_York.
